prompt:
I need the front end for Filingdesk. An in-house intake system built for a state Secretary of State's elections division, where qualifying staff enter and check the paperwork candidates submit to get on the primary ballot.

Who's using it: Rosalind Ferreira, a senior qualifying clerk in the elections division with nine election cycles behind her. She knows the qualifying statutes by heart and is training two seasonal clerks hired for the filing week.

What they're doing right now: It's day three of the five-day qualifying period, and the walk-in line is long. Rosalind is entering the filing of a first-time candidate for State House District 47. His declaration lists a residence address that the voter file puts in District 46, his chosen ballot name 'Bobby' doesn't match the name on his registration ('Roberto L. Quiñones'), and the qualifying fee check is $12 short because he paid last cycle's amount. She needs to record every document he handed over, have the system check each one against the statute, record which problems can be fixed before the noon Friday deadline and which would disqualify him, and print a deficiency notice for him to sign before he leaves the counter.

Submitted items: candidate oath (notarized), financial disclosure form, loyalty oath, fee check #2041 for $1,770.12 against a required $1,782.12, and an optional petition alternative with 0 signatures. Voter-file lookup returns precinct 46-012 and registration date 2019-08-03. Statutory rules: ballot name may use a nickname only with a sworn statement, fees are 6% of the office salary, and residency must be in the district at qualifying. 312 filings received so far this week across 140 offices, 41 with open deficiencies. Deadline: Friday, noon.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
